item.question: A bar is cut into 5 equal parts and 4 parts are shaded, so 4/5 of the bar is shaded. Now cut every part into 2 equal pieces. What fraction names the shaded part now? Has the shaded area changed?
steps: The bar has 5 equal parts and 4 of them are shaded, so the shaded part is 4/5.
Cut every part into 2 equal pieces. The whole now has 5 × 2 = 10 equal parts.
Each shaded part was cut into 2 pieces, so the shaded pieces are 4 × 2 = 8.
8 shaded pieces out of 10 equal pieces is the fraction 8/10.
Check the area: nothing was added to the colour and nothing was taken away. Only cut lines were drawn, so the shaded area is the same.
The same part of the whole has two names, 4/5 and 8/10. They are equivalent fractions.
item.answer: 8/10. The shaded area has not changed, so 4/5 = 8/10

item.question: A bar has 8 equal parts and 3 parts are shaded, so 3/8 of the bar is shaded. Cut every part into 2 equal pieces, and then, on a copy of the first bar, cut every part into 3 equal pieces. Write the two new fractions and find the pattern.
steps: The bar has 8 equal parts and 3 are shaded: 3/8.
Cut every part into 2 equal pieces. The shaded pieces are 3 × 2 = 6. The equal pieces in the whole are 8 × 2 = 16. The fraction is 6/16.
Cut every part of the first bar into 3 equal pieces. The shaded pieces are 3 × 3 = 9. The equal pieces in the whole are 8 × 3 = 24. The fraction is 9/24.
Look at the top numbers: 3, 6, 9. Look at the bottom numbers: 8, 16, 24.
From 3/8 to 6/16 the top and the bottom were both multiplied by 2. From 3/8 to 9/24 they were both multiplied by 3.

item.answer: 3/8 = 6/16 = 9/24. To make an equivalent fraction, multiply the top number and the bottom number by the same number
